author: Will Hammock
title: Local legend: Joe Ford, voice of Dacula Falcons football for 4 decades, dies - NewsBreak
text:
By Will Hammock ,
4 hours ago Joe Ford, right, poses for a photo with Chuck Warbington at the Dacula Athletics Hall of Fame celebration in 2013. By Special Photo Joe Ford was a fixture in Dacula for a number of reasons, but many remember him most for his voice.
For 40 years, Ford served as the announcer for Dacula High School football games and the community knew kickoff was near when his signature call of “You are now in Falcon Country” echoed across Barron Field. The Joe Ford Press Box at the Falcons’ high school stadium was named in his honor in 2014, and he was a member of the inaugural class for the Dacula Athletics Hall of Fame in 2013.
Community members recalled those memories and many more while mourning the loss of Ford, who died Monday afternoon after an extended illness, his friends said.
“Joe was always a valued classmate and a blessing to each of us, as well as to the town of Dacula,” Linda Davis Cox posted on social media.
“The local legend, ‘Voice of the Falcons,’ call to action on Friday night ‘You are now in Falcon Country’ will be missed,” Chuck Warbington said.
Ford attended Dacula School from 1955 through his graduation in 1967 and was a manager on the rural school’s first football team, in addition to serving as manager and statistician for the baseball and basketball teams from 1963-67.
He attended the Atlanta Broadcasting School and Gainesville Junior College, which led to a stint as a radio broadcaster for WGCO FM 102 in Buford and assisting Bob Joseph with state basketball playoff broadcasts in 1969. He also worked at his parents’ store, Tanner Ford Hardware, in downtown Dacula. He purchased the store from his parents in 1976 and ran the business until it closed in March 2012. His father opened the store in 1946.
Ford also was a volunteer baseball and basketball coach in the first Hebron Recreational League in 1968. He coached baseball, basketball and softball in the Hebron league until 1981.
He missed just just a few games during his four decades as Dacula’s football announcer. He began working in the booth at Dacula football games in 1972 as assistant to Cleve Langley, and took over the PA duties in 1974 through his retirement in 2014.
